recipes.name: Brown Sugar Instant Oatmeal Muffins
ingredients_raw: 2 packets instant maple and brown sugar oatmeal

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease 12 muffin cups.
Combine 3 tablespoons flour, brown sugar, and cinnamon in a small bowl. Use a pastry blender or two knives to cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Reserve.

Combine 1 3/4 cup flour, white sugar, baking powder, salt, and the instant oatmeal in a large bowl. Make a well in the center of the flour mixture; pour in the egg, milk, and oil. Stir just until moistened. Spoon batter into prepared muffin cups, filling each 2/3 full. Evenly sprinkle streusel topping over muffins.
Bake in preheated oven until toothpick inserted in center of muffin comes out clean, about 15 minutes. Cool on wire rack for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Brown Sugar Instant Oatmeal Muffins
raw_recipe.description: Instant maple and brown sugar oatmeal adds sweetness and texture to these sweet breakfast treats.

review.reviewBody: I gave this 4 stars just because i changed the recipe a little....the first time i made these they were super dense and not very sweet but still good...the second time i added nother egg, extra sugar and vanilla and they were excellent

I give this recipe 5 stars...I was looking for an apple & cinnamon recipe so I tried it using 4 packets. To the recipe I added an extra egg, 1/2 cup Zulka sugar, 2 TBS baking powder, 3 instant packets of apple cinnamon, 1/2 raisins, 4 TBS of ICBIN butter (including oil), 1 TBS lemon juice to milk, we love spices I used 1 TBS of vanilla flavoring, 1/2 TBS cinnamon, nutmeg and allspice. For topping... I reduced brown sugar to 2 TBS (because added sugar & my husband is a diabetic didn't want it to sweet), also added 1 packet to topping. My husband couldn't believe I used instant oatmeal...rated it an A+ not sweet at all very moist. My teen son was upset I used his favorite oatmeal to make muffins, but he gave a thumbs up. I made 18 muffins and cook it a little longer.

This was amazing!!! Made as a cake as well. The extra egg is a must. I added a can of peaches I'd cut up, and was out of milk so subbed half cup of the peach syrup and half sweet tea. Added extra brown sugar to topping and cake, as well as extra cinnamon and lots of ginger. Added crushed almonds to topping which was fabulous. If making a cake, will need to cook for a half hour or more. This would be good with apples or any fruit, fresh, canned or dried.

I read A LOT of reviews before making these so I added another egg and more sugar to the batter (1/2 c. total.) as suggested by others. Also, I used apple cinnamon instant oatmeal because that is what I had, so I added some cinnamon to the batter as well. No other changes. They are very attractive. They look like something you would get at a bakery and are delicious. I'm looking forward to trying these with other oatmeal flavors.

Definitely add another egg. I did and my muffins didn't come out dense or heavy at all. If you like your muffins on the sweeter side, then you might want to add more sugar. I just threw in about 2 more tbs or so and it was just the right amount of sweetness for me. When I bake and the recipe calls for milk, I use buttermilk instead (made my own - 1 tbs of vinegar + 1 cup of milk). Don't overmix the batter! Happy baking ^_^

I used regular oatmeal, brown sugar, and syrup instead of instant. Also, substituted brown sugar for the regular sugar and added an egg. I would double the streusel topping next time. Turned out great!
I loved it!! Came out very good!! Ate 4... Pregnant problems. Lol. The only thing different i did was add two eggs instead of 1 and instead of plain old milk, i used vanilla coconut almond milk

Family liked these, but I modified it based on suggestions of other reviewers. CHANGES: 1) subbed apple cinnamon applesauce for veg oil 2) used 1/2 cup sugar instead of 1/3 cup 3) added an extra egg 4) added 1/2 tsp vanilla & 1/2 tsp maple flavoring to batter 5) added closer to 1/2 tsp cinnamon to streusel topping. Giving 4 stars because it had to be tweaked, but is probably closer to a 4.5. Next time I might add a little more maple flavoring & some cinnamon to the batter., as it was a little bland for my son ( and me).

I made some of the changes others' suggested (one of my favorite things about allrecipes) - such as adding an additional egg and vanilla. I used brown sugar instead of white and a little more baking powder (1T). I also added a package of the oatmeal to the streusel topping since I had an extra one, and 2 mashed bananas to the mix. The muffins were light in texture and flavor and had nice high peaks - so they were very appealing in appearance too!

Good base recipe- I did add the extra egg, vanilla and a 1 tsp of cinnamon to the dry batter mix ( recommended by other reviewers ). We will be making them again and experimenting with other oatmeal flavors too! Thanks for sharing
Definetly add an extra egg and vanilla to the recipe. My steusal was a little wet, so I will reduce the butter to 1 1/2 next time for a more crumbly texture.
I also read reviews. It does need the extra egg sugar and vanilla. This made them very good. It wouldn't hurt to add extra spices. Over all pretty good breakfast muffin.
So good!
I followed the recipe but baked them 7 minutes longer. I love these! I had some instant oatmeal approaching the expire date and this recipe is perfect for using them up!
Added raisins, family loved them :)
I added another packet of oatmeal and another quarter cup of milk. 2 apple cranberry and one cranberry. We totally enjoyed them and will be making often with different flavors.
Not bad, a little dense for my liking. The kids didn't complain. I might adjust the recipe a bit next time.

I agree with other reviews about adding a second egg and vanilla. Perhaps more sugar in the muffin if you prefer on the sweeter side. The first time making, these we a bit dense. And dry. I used vanilla almond milk, but don't think that was the reason they seemed dry.

I wanted to make a half batch (6 muffins) and the calculator to adjust the recipe was WAY off base. It reduced the flour, sugar, and so on, BUT kept the original, 12-serving recipe portions of 2 packets of cereal, a full cup of milk, and 1/4 cup oil. I only added about 1/4 cup milk, recognizing that the batter was too wet, but they just weren't muffins.

I didn't even taste them. They're going out to the birds and squirrels.

My girls dispse oatmeal all of a sudden:-( I made these to hide the oatmeal and use it up. They LOVE it.... Round two just out of oven!!! 
I have used different flavors and had success each time
